items.detail:
The post writes "Against that, the paper's own general pipeline scored 502.0 on IOI 2025. Hengxi Liu scored 591.23 on the same problems." The paper is more specific: "Our general Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC reaches 304 without code-specific RL and 502.0 after five rounds of GenCorrect", and Figure 8a gives the round-by-round climb from 343.9 to 502.0. A reader comparing 502.0 against a human's contest score cannot tell from the post that the 502.0 side had five rounds and 200 generations per round behind it. "General pipeline" gestures at this but does not say it. Adding four words — "after five rounds of GenCorrect" — would fix it, and the job's own done-when line asked for exactly this distinction ("the GenCorrect contribution distinguished from post-training"). Not blocking: the sentence is used against the model, not for it, so the omission does not flatter the claim.

3 findings carried by reviewers against `data/proposals/gitspawn-ai-coding-agent-git-config-rce.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Fix the GitSpawn disclosure date before the post is written — Manifold's page carries Sep 1, not Sep 2

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-1.md`.

The candidate's summary says "the vulnerability class Manifold Security disclosed on 2026-09-02" and its why-now says the agents were "still unpatched at disclosure three days ago". Fetching https://www.manifold.security/blog/ai-coding-agents-git-hijack on 2026-09-05 returns a byline date of "Sep 1, 2026", and an independent search corroborates it — "On Monday, Sep 1, 2026, Manifold Security published a research post by Francisco Rosales that names a class called GitSpawn", with "four of the eight flaws remained unpatched as of September 1". 2026-09-02 is The Hacker News's publication date, not the disclosure date — the docket's own evidence block correctly dates the THN piece 2026-09-02, so the two look to have been merged. Fix: the authoring job should read the Manifold page's raw HTML, take the disclosure date from it, and keep the THN date attached to THN. The why-now's "still unpatched at disclosure three days ago" needs the same correction.

### "Eight agents were reported affected" is eight findings across seven agents

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-2.md`.

The GitSpawn candidate's summary says "Eight agents were reported affected" and then lists seven products (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI and Desktop, Cursor, goose, Hermes Agent, Qwen Code, Grok Build). Manifold's table does have eight rows, but Claude Code occupies two of them — the core.fsmonitor path (patched 2.1.196) and the ultrareview path (unpatched at 2.1.252). Independent coverage counts it the same way — "GitSpawn, Seven Coding Agents", and "four of the eight flaws remained unpatched as of September 1". Fix: the post should say eight findings across seven agents, which also makes the "four fixed, four unpatched" split parse correctly.

### The docket's account of what The Hacker News says about CVE-2026-71963 may itself be wrong

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-3.md`.

The candidate flags a discrepancy: "the Manifold table as extracted attributes CVE-2026-71963 to Hermes Agent; The Hacker News attributes CVE-2026-71963 to Grok Build". Fetching the THN piece on 2026-09-05 returns "VulnCheck assigned CVE-2026-71963, according to Manifold" in the Hermes Agent passage, not the Grok Build one — i.e. the two sources may agree, and the disagreement may be an artifact of the extractor. This changes nothing about the required action, since the docket already instructs the authoring job to check each CVE against MITRE/NVD directly, but the post should not assert that the two outlets disagree without re-reading both in raw HTML first.

items.detail:
`data/proposals/substituted-rows-report-as-retirements.md` says "`MATERIAL_KINDS` at `lib/changes.mjs:35` carries it onto the home changed feed". It does not: a repository-wide grep for `MATERIAL_KINDS` returns exactly two hits, its own `export` at `lib/changes.mjs:35` and this proposal's sentence — the constant has no consumer anywhere in `lib/`, `app/`, `pulse/` or `scripts/`. What actually puts the line on the home feed is `lib/site.mjs:118`, `changes: changedFeed(changeLines, { entries: corpus.entry })`, which passes every line of `changes.jsonl` through unfiltered; the word itself comes from `describeChange` at `lib/changes.mjs:173`. The outcome the proposal describes is real and I confirmed it independently — only the gate it names is the wrong one, and whoever picks up the proposed machinery job would go looking at a dead constant for a filter that is not there. Fixing the sentence to name `lib/site.mjs:118` is the whole correction.

items.detail:
The evidence file's header says the raw transcript is a "node fetch+strip+count script, 2026-09-03; the huggingface.co/meta-models org page was fetched twice because its activity feed renders intermittently". Grepping "^=== https" over data/reviews/evidence/verify-meta-spark-weights-pending-status.raw.txt returns 11 fetch blocks and huggingface.co/meta-models appears exactly once (line 22). The underlying observation is real — that page's stripped length was 2556 in the transcript and 2548 when I fetched it myself minutes later — but as written the sentence describes a second fetch the transcript does not contain. Either capture both fetches, or say it plainly ("the page was fetched in both this run and the earlier one and rendered differently; only this run's is captured"). This is the same narrative-outruns-transcript shape the previous pass flagged, at much smaller scale, which is why it is carried rather than blocked on.

items.detail:
`data/sources/README.md` opens by enumerating what `registry.json` declares — "URL, the fields it yields, which field is the row id ..., `fetch_every_days`, `expected_change_days`, an optional `mints` mapping, its robots/terms check result, and the date that check was made". The new optional `declined_fields` key is absent from that list, though the module docstring in `pulse/lib/registry.mjs` was updated to name it. A reader who opens the directory's own README to learn the registry's shape will not learn the key exists — a mild instance of the exact "you cannot tell what has been decided" problem this change was made to end. Fix: extend that sentence with "the optional `declined_fields` refusals (a path this repo has looked at and deliberately does not carry, each with its `decided_on` date and the measurement behind it)".
